title: Amogh Lila EXPOSED: Are Scriptures Really the Absolute Truth?
tags: why science is better than religion
description:
In this video from Pale Blue Thoughts, we debunk the claims made by Amogh Lila Prabhu, a popular ISKCON monk and motivational speaker who often belittles science while freely using the products of science. His viral reel mocks atomic theory by twisting the contributions of John Dalton, J.J. Thomson, Rutherford, Bohr, and Schrödinger, claiming science is always “wrong” while scriptures remain unchanged—and therefore “true.”

But science is not about unchanging dogma. It is about evidence, experiments, and progress. Dalton’s model wasn’t “wrong”—it was foundational. Each discovery refined our understanding: Thomson found electrons, Rutherford discovered the nucleus, Bohr explained quantized orbits, and Schrödinger gave us the quantum mechanical model. That’s how science grows—through correction, refinement, and falsifiability.

Amogh Lila also uses the fallacies of appeal to authority and appeal to antiquity, claiming scriptures are “bonafide sources of knowledge.” But scriptures across religions contain errors, contradictions, and outdated cosmologies—from geocentrism to flat-earth models. Science, by contrast, has given us vaccines, antibiotics, relativity, evolution, quantum mechanics, plate tectonics, and modern technology—progress no scripture ever predicted.

👉 If you’ve searched for Amogh Lila Prabhu debunked, ISKCON monk pseudoscience, Amogh Lila vs science, atomic theory explained, religion vs science debate, appeal to antiquity fallacy — this video gives you the scientific breakdown.

Then he uses this aspects of science to glorify his scripture by saying that it has been unchanged for so long so it must be the truth. In reality, John Dalton was not necessarily wrong in his time. But his model was a simple and early representation of the atom and subsequent discoveries and models refined our understanding. John Dalton, JJ Thompson, Ernest to the four, Neils Bor and Irving Shortinger all made significant contributions to our understanding of the atom. each building upon the work of their predecessors. Dalton's bill model proposed that atoms were indivisible indestructible particles. He suggested that each element was composed of unique atoms and chemical reactions involved the rearrangement of these atoms. While Dalton's theory was a groundbreaking idea and a significant departure from earlier models, it was overly simplistic and did not account for the internal structure of the atoms. Thompson's experiments with cathode rays led to the discovery of electrons, negatively charged subatomic particles. He proposed the plum pudding model in which electrons were embedded in a positively charged pudding or matrix. This model recognized the presence of subatomic particles within the atom but did not provide a detailed atomic structure. Ratherford's famous gold foil experiment revealed that atoms had a nucleus at their center which was densely packed with positively charged protons. He proposed the planetary model of the atom where electrons orbited the nucleus in a manner similar to planets around the sun. This model introduced the concept of a central nucleus and greatly advanced our understanding of our atomic structure. Then came along Neils Boore whose atomic model was like a simplified picture of how atoms work especially the tiny particles inside them called electrons. He postulated the energy levels of electrons with specific and fixed orbits quantized energy and stability. So B's model was like a simple staircase model for atoms where electrons can only exist on certain steps and can jump between them releasing specific colors of light when they do. It helped us understand some basics about how atoms work. This model was a great way to understand what goes beneath everything, but it mainly worked well for simple atoms like hydrogen. For more complicated atoms, we needed a better model called quantum mechanics. Shinger along with other quantum physicists developed the quantum mechanical model of the atom. This model describes electrons not as particles with definite orbits but as wave functions or electron clouds that represent the probability of finding electrons in specific regions around the nucleus. Shortinger's model successfully explained the behavior of electrons in atoms and provided a more accurate description than the previous models. Now, John Dalton's model was a significant step in understanding the nature of chemical elements and reactions, but it was relatively simple and did not address the internal structure of atoms. He wasn't wrong per se. Subsequent scientists like Thompson, Rotherford, Bar and Schroinger built upon Dalton's ideas and experimental evidence to develop more refined atomic models. While Dton's model was foundational, it was not comprehensive and later models provided a more accurate and detailed picture of the atomic structure and behavior. That is how science progresses. We start from a simple understanding of something. Then as we conduct more experiments, we develop a bigger and deeper understanding of it. Gurus and science deniers often want to reach the final answer without the intermediate steps. That just doesn't work. You can't sit and meditate and hope for the right answer if you haven't followed the process. To build a house, you need to build it brick by brick. It cannot appear poof out of thin air on one fine day. There is a journey that one needs to take to reach the final destination. We may take some wrong turns during the journey but if we keep at it, we shall reach the target one day. I have heard some other spiritual gurus take the case of Newton and Einstein to make a similar point. Newton proposed the theory of gravity and Einstein came and proved Newton was wrong. Newtonian theory wasn't wrong and we can still use it almost everywhere and can even use it to make predictions even today. The orbit and motion of Uranus when it was first discovered by William Herschel were calculated using Newton's laws of gravitation. The discovery of Neptune is a remarkable example of the power of mathematical prediction based on Newtonian physics. The planet Uranus after its discovery exhibited slight irregularities in its orbit that could not be explained by the gravitational influence of known celestial bodies. French mathematician Urban Lea and British mathematician John Couch Adams independently calculated the existence and position of an unseen planet that could explain these irregularities. While the discoveries of Uranus and Neptune themselves were not directly made using Newtonian physics, the understanding of their orbits, motions, and the prediction of Neptune's existence were strongly influenced by Newton's laws of gravitation. So, Newton wasn't wrong. His theory can still be used to predict the motion and orbit of all celestial bodies except the ones which revolve close to a huge mass, say Mercury's orbit around the sun. That is where Einstein refined and I mean refined Newtonian theories with his relativity theories. Newton wasn't wrong. Einstein enhanced the accuracy of the theory further. Further in science there are no authorities or gurus. Even a patent office clerk has the chance to dethrone the father of physics. All he needs to provide is evidence. The phrase, "Science keeps correcting itself," underscores his commitment to seeking out the truth. Over time, scientific theories evolve to better explain the natural world based on new evidence. Think about the theory of plate tectonics. Initially met with skepticism, it is now widely accepted as a fundamental concept in geology, illustrating science's self-correcting nature. Think about the theory of evolution. When it came out, it created such an uproar in the scientific community. But today, it is accepted as the best explanation for the biodiversity of life. Well, let me correct the statement. Accepted by anyone who cares to understand it and does not cling on to religious scriptures. Same goes for Einstein's special and general relativity theories and quantum mechanics. I have often spoken about how Einstein's theory was met with much skepticism and a certain Arthur Readington conducted a famous experiment during a solar eclipse which proved Einstein was right. He did it to disprove Einstein but had to eat the umbories which were wrong and had to be replaced. Geocentrism was one. The ancient view that the earth was at the center of the universe with celestial objects including the sun and planets orbiting around it was the prevailing model for many centuries. This theory was replaced by the heliocentric model proposed by Copernicus and later refined by Kepla and Galio which correctly placed the sun at the center of the solar system. In the 18th and early 19th centuries, the caloric theory suggested that heat was a fluid-like substance called caloric that flowed from hotter to colder objects. This theory was later replaced by the kinetic theory of heat which explained heat as the motion of atomic particles and laid the foundation for a modern understanding of thermodynamics. The flogiston theory popular in the 18th century suggested that substances contain a hypothetical floiston that was released during combustion explaining why things burned and rusted. This theory was replaced by Antonine Lavosia's work on the conservation of mass and the identification of oxygen as the key component in combustion reactions. In the 19th century, it was widely believed that there existed a medium called the lumiferous ether through which light waves traveled. similar to sound waves in air. However, experiments such as the Michaelelsson model experiment failed to detect the ether leading to the development of Albert Einstein's theory of special relativity which fundamentally changed our understanding of space and time. Last but not the least, who can forget how we understood the shape of the earth in ancient times. We all envisaged a flat model of our earth. Even though philosophers like Pythagoras and Aristotle concluded through their observations that the earth was not flat but spherical in shape. Today we have conclusive evidence that the earth is in fact a spherical ball flying around the sun. Today's modern technologies like GPS and satellite communication would only work if the earth were a sphere. So why do science makes mistakes? Because humans make mistakes and humans do science. And the less knowledge we have, the more chance to make mistakes. But as we improve our understanding of something, the tendency to make mistakes grows lesser and the ability to grow deeper into a subject increases. Simple logic. Pity how some gurus don't have this understanding. So how did we evolve to get a better understanding of our universe and nature using science? The answer lies in a simple yet not so simple eightletter word. Evidence. Evidence acquired through rigorous observations. Science in the last few hundred years that it has been around has given people vaccines, antibiotics, better transportation, communication systems, different forms of entertainment, better health and living standards, more food, clean water, you name it. things no scriptures have been able to provide in thousands of years. While science has led humans in the path of progress, the scriptures have tied them up in the centuries they were written in. It's a pity that a person who was once a computer engineer has resorted to eating the fruits of science and cutting the roots of science. And I have sympathies towards the thought process of the audience who hoot and clap when they hear their acharia spout nonsense. The Pharisees that the Maha Prabhu uses here are appeal to authority and appeal to antiquity. I have done a video on appeal to authority which I will link it up here and in the description. When someone tries to validate a claim or belief by asserting that it is supported by an authoritative source in this case scriptures, he's doing it without providing any substantial evidence or reasoning to support the claim. In this fallacy, the person is essentially saying because the scriptures say so, it must be true without considering alternate source of knowledge, critical thinking or empirical evidence. It dismisses other forms of knowledge such as scientific observation, historical research or philosophical reasoning and relies solely on the authority of scriptures. The appeal to antiquity is a mistake in thinking where someone believes that something is good or right just because it's old or has been around for a long time. In other words, they think that if something has been done or believed for a very long time, it must be true or valuable. However, this is not always the case. Just because something is old doesn't mean it's correct or the best option. People used to believe and did so many things in the past that we now know are not accurate or outdated. So it's important to evaluate ideas and practices based on evidence and reason rather than simply relying on their age. So to cut the long story short, while scriptures simply claim to offer valuable guidance in matters of spirituality and morality, they are not the ultimate source of knowledge, especially when it comes to understanding the natural world. Science with its empirical foundation and capacity for selfcorrection stands as the foremost source for unraveling the mysteries of the universe and improving our lives.
